title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
text:
Overview

How are economic deprivation and socioeconomic disadvantage spatially distributed across U.S. counties, and how are they associated with health outcomes, environmental exposures, and healthcare access?


Objectives








Objective
Question
Sections




1. Measure economic deprivation
Can a transparent county EDI be built from Atlas indicators, and is it robust to how it is weighted?
3


2. Identify spatial inequality
Is deprivation clustered, where are the hot and cold spots, and how much of the inequality lies between states and regions?
5 to 7


3. Explain geographic disparities
What demographic and regional characteristics go with deprivation (Model 1), and how is deprivation associated with health (Model 2)?
8 to 12





Hypotheses







Hypothesis
Statistical test




H1: Economic deprivation is spatially clustered across U.S. counties.
Global Moran’s I


H2: High-deprivation counties form statistically significant geographic hotspots.
LISA (FDR) and Getis-Ord Gi*


H3: Economic deprivation is positively associated with adverse health outcomes.
OLS, SAR, SEM, SDM with impacts


H4: The deprivation-health relationship varies geographically.
GW correlation, GWR, MGWR


H5: Environmental burdens are disproportionately concentrated in economically deprived counties.
Bivariate LISA and regression

The EDI is built from CHR measures only. The SVI socioeconomic theme is kept out of the index so that it can serve as an independent check, and no EDI component is used again as a predictor in a model that has the EDI on either side.


Workflow (guideline step in brackets)







Step
What we do




Data [1, 2]
SQL extract from the Atlas database; documented reference years


Cleaning [3]
FIPS, duplicates, missingness by variable and state, scale and outlier checks, geometry join


Index [guideline Section 3]
Equal-weighted and PCA-based EDI; leave-one-out and add-one sensitivity; comparison with SVI


EDA [4]
Descriptive statistics, distributions, correlation matrix, scatterplots, seven choropleths


Autocorrelation [5]
Global Moran’s I for the EDI and its components; Queen and KNN weights


Clusters [5]
LISA with FDR and Gi*; inequality between and within states and regions


Deprivation and health [6]
Bivariate LISA: EDI against diabetes, premature death, and PM2.5


Model 1 [guideline Section 5]
What goes with deprivation: OLS, LM tests, SAR, SEM


Model 2 [7]
Deprivation and health: OLS, SAR, SEM, SDM; direct, indirect, and total impacts; four outcomes


Local models [8]
Geographically weighted correlation, GWR, MGWR


Machine learning [9]
Linear, Ridge, Elastic Net, Random Forest, XGBoost; random versus state-blocked CV; TreeSHAP


Report [10]
Hypothesis summary, decision log, limitations



Caveats. County associations are ecological, not individual causal effects. CHR measures are release-year values, several of them model-based, and do not all refer to the same data year. The Atlas database does not hold median income, PLACES, CDC WONDER mortality, overdose, cancer, or soil layers at the time of writing, so those parts of the guideline are listed as extensions. The county shapefile covers the contiguous United States, so Alaska and Hawaii are not in the study region. Every number below is computed in this notebook.

Setup
Installation. This notebook needs installation option 5 (core, spatial analysis, spatial statistics, geostatistics and remote sensing): pip install "geolattice[remote-sensing]". See “Installation options” in the GeoLattice README. It also uses statsmodels, which no GeoLattice option installs: pip install statsmodels.

section: Data: what the Atlas database holds
text:
Data: what the Atlas database holds
The guideline’s first step is to choose the geography and period and to document the reference year of every variable. The database stores every source as long county_indicators rows, so one query shows which dataset-years exist. The analysis is a cross-section centered on 2022: SVI 2022, Census PEP 2022, and the CHR 2024 release, which is the CHR release closest to those inputs.


Code
con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
catalog = pd.read_sql("SELECT dataset_name, temporal_coverage FROM dataset_catalog", con)
coverage = pd.read_sql(
    "SELECT d.dataset_name, i.year, COUNT(DISTINCT i.fips) AS counties "
    "FROM county_indicators AS i JOIN dataset_catalog AS d USING (dataset_id) "
    "GROUP BY d.dataset_name, i.year",
    con,
)
loaded = coverage.pivot(index="dataset_name", columns="year", values="counties").fillna(0).astype(int)
display(Markdown("**Counties with data, by dataset and year**"))
display(loaded)
not_loaded = sorted(set(catalog["dataset_name"]) - set(loaded.index) - {"presidential_election", "atlas_eda_pipeline"})
print("catalogued but not loaded as county indicators:", ", ".join(not_loaded))

# analysis name -> (dataset, variable, year)
SPEC = {name: ("county_health_rankings", var, CHR_YEAR) for name, (var, _rev) in EDI_SPEC.items()}
SPEC.update({
    "income_inequality": ("county_health_rankings", "Income Inequality", CHR_YEAR),
    "diabetes": ("county_health_rankings", "Diabetes Prevalence", CHR_YEAR),
    "premature_death": ("county_health_rankings", "Premature Death", CHR_YEAR),

    "pop": ("census_demography", "POP", CENSUS_YEAR),

    "pct_65plus": ("census_demography", "PCT_65PLUS", CENSUS_YEAR),

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
text:
Cleaning and integration
The guideline’s Step 3 checklist: five-character FIPS, duplicate county-year records, missingness by variable and by state, consistent scales, implausible values, and the join to county geometry. Outcomes are never imputed. Counties with a missing model input are dropped (complete cases), and the cell reports how many and where.


Code
# 1) FIPS format and duplicates
long["fips"] = long["fips"].astype(str).str.zfill(5)
assert long["fips"].str.fullmatch(r"\d{5}").all(), "FIPS codes must be five digits"
n_dup = int(long.duplicated(["fips", "dataset_name", "variable", "year"]).sum())
print(f"five-digit FIPS: OK  |  duplicate county-variable-year rows: {n_dup}")

wide = long.pivot_table(index="fips", columns=["dataset_name", "variable", "year"], values="value")
table = pd.DataFrame(index=wide.index)
for name, key in SPEC.items():
    table[name] = wide[key].to_numpy()

# 2) Consistent scales: CHR proportions -> percent; reverse-code attainment; derived change
for name, (_var, reverse) in EDI_SPEC.items():
    table[name] = 100 * (1 - table[name]) if reverse else 100 * table[name]
table["diabetes_pct"] = 100 * table["diabetes"]
table["uninsured_pct"] = 100 * table["uninsured"]
table["pop_change"] = 100 * (table["pop"] / table["pop_base"] - 1)

# 3) Join geometry (contiguous United States)
shp = gpd.read_file(SHP)
shp["fips"] = shp["FIPS"].astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)
merged = shp.merge(table.reset_index(), on="fips", how="left")
merged["region"] = merged["STATE"].map(STATE_REGION)
assert merged["region"].notna().all(), "every state needs a Census region"

edi_cols = list(EDI_SPEC)
need = [*edi_cols, "income_inequality", *OUTCOMES, "pm25", "uninsured_pct", "svi", "svi_ses", *DEMOG]
miss_var = merged[need].isna().sum()
display(Markdown("**Missing values by variable (CONUS counties in the shapefile)**"))
display(miss_var[miss_var > 0].sort_values(ascending=False).rename("counties missing").to_frame())

incomplete = merged[need].isna().any(axis=1)
miss_state = (
    pd.DataFrame({"counties": merged.groupby("STATE").size(), "dropped": incomplete.groupby(merged["STATE"]).sum()})
    .assign(pct_dropped=lambda d: 100 * d["dropped"] / d["counties"])
    .sort_values("pct_dropped", ascending=False)
)
display(Markdown("**States losing the largest share of counties to missing inputs**"))
display(miss_state.head(8).style.format({"pct_dropped": "{:.0f}"}))

counties = merged.loc[~incomplete].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
coords = np.column_stack([counties.geometry.centroid.x, counties.geometry.centroid.y])

# 4) Plausibility: ranges and extreme values
pct_like = [*edi_cols, "diabetes_pct", "uninsured_pct", "pct_65plus", "pct_under18", "pct_rural",
            "pct_nhblack", "pct_hispanic", "pct_aian"]
assert ((counties[pct_like] >= 0) & (counties[pct_like] <= 100)).all().all(), "percentages outside 0-100"
assert counties[["svi", "svi_ses"]].apply(lambda s: s.between(0, 1)).all().all(), "SVI ranks outside 0-1"
z_all = (counties[need] - counties[need].mean()) / counties[need].std(ddof=0)
extreme = (z_all.abs() > 5).sum()
display(Markdown("**Counties more than 5 SD from the mean (kept, but worth knowing about)**"))
display(extreme[extreme > 0].rename("counties").to_frame().T)

all_missing_states = miss_state.index[miss_state["pct_dropped"] == 100].tolist()
display(Markdown(
    f"Study region: **{len(counties):,}** of **{len(merged):,}** CONUS counties have every input "
    f"(**{int(incomplete.sum())}** dropped, **{incomplete.mean() * 100:.1f}%**). "
    f"The variables with the most gaps are **{miss_var.idxmax()}** ({int(miss_var.max())}) and "
    f"**{miss_var.sort_values().index[-2]}** ({int(miss_var.sort_values().iloc[-2])}), which CHR suppresses for small populations, "
    f"so the dropped counties are mostly small and rural. "
    + (f"States with no usable county: **{', '.join(all_missing_states)}**. " if all_missing_states else "")
    + f"Projected CRS: {'NAD83 Albers (metres)' if counties.crs and counties.crs.is_projected else 'check CRS'}."
))

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
text:
Constructing the Economic Deprivation Index
Each indicator is standardized, \(Z_{ij} = (X_{ij} - \bar X_j) / SD(X_j)\), after the two attainment measures have been reverse-coded so that higher always means more deprived. The equal-weighted index is the mean of the six z-scores:
\[EDI_i = \frac{1}{p}\sum_{j=1}^{p} Z^{*}_{ij}\]
The guideline recommends computing a PCA-based index as well and comparing county rankings. Three further checks are added: dropping each component in turn, adding income inequality (which the guideline flags as context-dependent), and comparing the result with the SVI socioeconomic theme, which is built from different (ACS) inputs.


Code
def zscore(frame):
    return (frame - frame.mean()) / frame.std(ddof=0)


Z = zscore(counties[edi_cols])
counties["edi"] = Z.mean(axis=1)

# PCA weights: first principal component of the standardized components
_, sing, Vt = np.linalg.svd(Z.to_numpy(), full_matrices=False)

        "PC1 loading": loadings, "equal weight": 1 / np.sqrt(len(edi_cols)),
        "r with EDI": [np.corrcoef(Z[c], counties["edi"])[0, 1] for c in edi_cols],
    }
).rename(index=EDI_LABELS)

alpha_cron = len(edi_cols) / (len(edi_cols) - 1) * (1 - np.trace(Z.cov(ddof=0).to_numpy()) / Z.sum(axis=1).var(ddof=0))

    ta, tb = set(a.index[a >= a.quantile(q)]), set(b.index[b >= b.quantile(q)])
    return len(ta & tb) / len(ta)

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
text:
Is deprivation spatially clustered? (H1)
Global Moran’s I with row-standardized Queen contiguity and 999 permutations, as the guideline specifies. Counties left without a neighbor after the complete-case filter are linked to their nearest county. The statistic is computed for the EDI, each component, and the two alternative indices, and repeated with k-nearest-neighbor weights as a check.


Code
def attach_islands(w, xy):
    # Link each island to its nearest non-island county, both ways, then row-standardise.
    ids = list(w.id_order)
    pos = {i: k for k, i in enumerate(ids)}
    islands = set(w.islands())
    neighbors = {i: list(w.neighbors[i]) for i in ids}
    if not islands:
        return W(neighbors, ids=ids, transform="row")
    tree = cKDTree(xy)
    for isl in islands:
        _, idxs = tree.query(xy[pos[isl]], k=min(25, len(ids)))
        for j in np.atleast_1d(idxs):
            other = ids[int(j)]
            if other == isl or other in islands:
                continue
            if other not in neighbors[isl]:
                neighbors[isl].append(other)
            if isl not in neighbors[other]:
                neighbors[other].append(isl)
            break
    return W(neighbors, ids=ids, transform="row")


w_raw = Queen(counties, transform="row")
w = attach_islands(w_raw, coords)
w_knn = KNN(coords, k=6, transform="row")
print(w.summary())

                 **{c: EDI_LABELS[c] for c in edi_cols}}
rows, morans = [], {}
for col, label in moran_targets.items():
    v = counties[col].to_numpy(float)
    mi = Moran(v, w, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED)
    mk_ = Moran(v, w_knn, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED)
    morans[col] = mi
    rows.append({"variable": label, "I_queen": mi.I, "z": mi.z_score, "p_value": mi.p_value,
                 "I_knn6": mk_.I, "p_knn6": mk_.p_value})
moran_tbl = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("variable")

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
section: Where are the deprivation hot spots? (H2)
text:
Where are the deprivation hot spots? (H2)
Local Moran’s I classifies each county as High-High, Low-Low, High-Low, or Low-High. With about 2,900 simultaneous tests the p-values are adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate, using 9,999 permutations so that the adjusted p-values have enough resolution. Getis-Ord Gi* (analytic, FDR-adjusted) is mapped alongside as a second definition of a hot spot.


Code
def gi_group(label: str) -> str:
    lab = str(label)
    if lab.startswith("Hot"):
        return "Hot spot"
    if lab.startswith("Cold"):
        return "Cold spot"
    return "Not significant"


y_edi = counties["edi"].to_numpy(float)
lisa_unc = local_moran_clusters(y_edi, w, permutations=PERM_LOCAL, correction="none", alpha=ALPHA, seed=SEED)
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    # The resolution warning for FDR is silenced; the counts below show how many counties survive.
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
    lisa = local_moran_clusters(y_edi, w, permutations=PERM_LOCAL, correction="fdr", alpha=ALPHA, seed=SEED)
gi = getis_ord_gi(y_edi, w, star=True, inference="analytic", alpha=ALPHA, seed=SEED)
counties["lisa_edi"] = list(lisa.labels)
counties["gi_edi"] = [gi_group(x) for x in gi.labels]

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
section: How much of the inequality is between places?
text:
How much of the inequality is between places?
Clustering maps do not say how large the geographic gaps are. Decomposing the county variance of the EDI into a between-group and a within-group part gives a direct measure: the share that would remain if every county took its state (or region) mean. A population-weighted version asks the same question for people instead of counties. Diabetes prevalence is decomposed the same way for comparison.


Code
def between_share(values, groups, weights=None):
    # Share of (weighted) variance that lies between group means.
    v = np.asarray(values, float)
    wt = np.ones_like(v) if weights is None else np.asarray(weights, float)
    grand = np.average(v, weights=wt)
    total = np.average((v - grand) ** 2, weights=wt)
    frame = pd.DataFrame({"v": v, "w": wt, "g": np.asarray(groups)})
    gm = frame.groupby("g").apply(lambda d: np.average(d["v"], weights=d["w"]), include_groups=False)
    gw = frame.groupby("g")["w"].sum()
    return float(np.sum(gw * (gm - grand) ** 2) / gw.sum() / total)


dec_rows = []
for col, label in [("edi", "EDI"), ("diabetes_pct", "Diabetes prevalence")]:
    for wname, wt in [("counties", None), ("population", counties["pop"])]:
        dec_rows.append({
            "variable": label, "weighted by": wname,
            "between regions": between_share(counties[col], counties["region"], wt),
            "between states": between_share(counties[col], counties["STATE"], wt),
        })
dec_tbl = pd.DataFrame(dec_rows).set_index(["variable", "weighted by"])
dec_tbl["within states"] = 1 - dec_tbl["between states"]
display(dec_tbl.style.format("{:.0%}"))

state_tbl = counties.groupby("STATE").agg(
    region=("region", "first"), counties=("edi", "size"), mean_edi=("edi", "mean"),
    sd_within=("edi", "std"), min_edi=("edi", "min"), max_edi=("edi", "max"),
)
state_tbl["range"] = state_tbl["max_edi"] - state_tbl["min_edi"]
state_tbl = state_tbl[state_tbl["counties"] >= 5].sort_values("mean_edi")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 4.2), constrained_layout=True)
x = np.arange(len(state_tbl))
ax.vlines(x, state_tbl["min_edi"], state_tbl["max_edi"], color="0.75", lw=2)
ax.scatter(x, state_tbl["mean_edi"], c=[REGION_COLORS[r] for r in state_tbl["region"]], s=28, zorder=3)
ax.axhline(0, color="0.4", lw=0.8)
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(state_tbl.index, rotation=90, fontsize=7)
ax.set_ylabel("EDI")
ax.set_title("State mean EDI (dot) and county range within each state (line)")
ax.legend(handles=[Patch(color=c, label=r) for r, c in REGION_COLORS.items()], frameon=False, fontsize=8, ncol=4)
plt.show()

e = dec_tbl.loc[("EDI", "counties")]

    f"**{e['between states'] * 100:.0f}%**, so **{e['within states'] * 100:.0f}%** of the inequality is between counties of the same state. "
    f"Weighted by population the between-state share is **{dec_tbl.loc[('EDI', 'population'), 'between states'] * 100:.0f}%**. "

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
section: Deprivation, health, and environmental burden across county lines (H3, H5)
text:
Deprivation, health, and environmental burden across county lines (H3, H5)
Bivariate Moran’s I relates the EDI of a county to the average of another variable in its neighbors, and bivariate LISA shows where that association is located. Three pairs follow the guideline’s questions: EDI with neighboring diabetes prevalence, EDI with neighboring premature death, and EDI with neighboring PM2.5.


Code
BV_TARGETS = {"diabetes_pct": "diabetes", "premature_death": "premature death", "pm25": "PM2.5"}
BV_NAMES = {"HH": "High EDI, high neighbors", "LL": "Low EDI, low neighbors",
            "HL": "High EDI, low neighbors", "LH": "Low EDI, high neighbors", "Not significant": "Not significant"}
z_edi = (y_edi - y_edi.mean()) / y_edi.std()
bv_rows, bv_counts = [], {}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.4), constrained_layout=True, dpi=110)
for ax, (col, name) in zip(axes, BV_TARGETS.items()):
    v = counties[col].to_numpy(float)
    zv = (v - v.mean()) / v.std()
    g = MoranBV(z_edi, zv, w, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED)
    loc = Moran_Local_BV(y_edi, v, w, permutations=PERM_LOCAL, seed=SEED, alpha=ALPHA, fdr=True)
    lab = np.array(["Not significant" if x == "NS" else x for x in loc.labels])
    counties[f"bv_{col}"] = lab
    bv_counts[name] = pd.Series(lab).value_counts()
    bv_rows.append({"pair": f"EDI vs neighboring {name}", "bivariate I": g.I, "p_value": g.p_value,
                    "aspatial r": float(np.corrcoef(y_edi, v)[0, 1])})
    for l, color in LISA_COLORS.items():
        part = counties[lab == l]
        if len(part):
            part.plot(ax=ax, color=color, edgecolor="none", linewidth=0)
    ax.set_title(f"Bivariate LISA: EDI and neighboring {name}", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_axis_off()
axes[0].legend(handles=[Patch(color=c, label=BV_NAMES[l]) for l, c in LISA_COLORS.items()],
               loc="lower left", fontsize=7, frameon=False)
plt.show()

bv_tbl = pd.DataFrame(bv_rows).set_index("pair")
display(bv_tbl.style.format({"bivariate I": "{:.3f}", "p_value": "{:.4f}", "aspatial r": "{:.3f}"}))
bv_cnt = pd.DataFrame(bv_counts).reindex(["HH", "LL", "HL", "LH", "Not significant"]).fillna(0).astype(int)
bv_cnt.index = [BV_NAMES[i] for i in bv_cnt.index]
display(bv_cnt)

edi_q = pd.qcut(counties["edi"], 5, labels=["Q1 least", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4", "Q5 most"])
grad = counties.groupby(edi_q, observed=True)[[*OUTCOMES, "pm25", "uninsured_pct"]].mean()
display(Markdown("**Means by EDI quintile**"))
display(grad.style.format({"diabetes_pct": "{:.1f}", "premature_death": "{:,.0f}", "life_expectancy": "{:.1f}",
                           "poor_mental_days": "{:.2f}", "pm25": "{:.2f}", "uninsured_pct": "{:.1f}"}))

pm_hh_states = counties.loc[counties["bv_pm25"] == "HH", "STATE"].value_counts().head(4)
pm_hl_states = counties.loc[counties["bv_pm25"] == "HL", "STATE"].value_counts().head(4)
b = bv_tbl["bivariate I"]
display(Markdown(
    f"Bivariate Moran's I is **{b.iloc[0]:.3f}** for diabetes and **{b.iloc[1]:.3f}** for premature death: deprived counties sit among "
    f"neighbors with worse health. From the least to the most deprived quintile, diabetes prevalence rises from "
    f"**{grad['diabetes_pct'].iloc[0]:.1f}%** to **{grad['diabetes_pct'].iloc[-1]:.1f}%** and life expectancy falls from "
    f"**{grad['life_expectancy'].iloc[0]:.1f}** to **{grad['life_expectancy'].iloc[-1]:.1f}** years. "
    f"For PM2.5 the association is much weaker (bivariate I = **{b.iloc[2]:.3f}**, aspatial r = **{bv_tbl['aspatial r'].iloc[2]:.3f}**): "
    f"**{int(bv_cnt.loc[BV_NAMES['HH'], 'PM2.5'])}** deprived counties have high-PM2.5 neighbors ("
    + ", ".join(f"{s} {n}" for s, n in pm_hh_states.items())
    + f") but **{int(bv_cnt.loc[BV_NAMES['HL'], 'PM2.5'])}** deprived counties have low-PM2.5 neighbors ("
    + ", ".join(f"{s} {n}" for s, n in pm_hl_states.items())

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
section: Model 1: what goes with economic deprivation?
text:
Model 1: what goes with economic deprivation?
\[EDI_i = f(\text{demography, rurality, region})\]
The dependent variable is the EDI. Predictors are population change since 2010, age composition, rural share, racial and ethnic composition, and Census region (Northeast as the reference). None of them is an EDI component, which avoids the circular model the guideline warns about. Continuous predictors are standardized. OLS is fitted first, Lagrange Multiplier tests indicate the form of spatial dependence, and spatial lag and spatial error models follow. The Durbin model is reserved for Model 2, because spatially lagged region dummies are nearly collinear with the dummies themselves.


Code
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor


def standardize(a):
    a = np.asarray(a, float)
    return (a - a.mean(axis=0)) / a.std(axis=0, ddof=0)


region_dummies = pd.get_dummies(counties["region"], dtype=float)[["Midwest", "South", "West"]]
X1 = np.column_stack([standardize(counties[DEMOG]), region_dummies.to_numpy()])
names1 = [*DEMOG, *[f"region_{r}" for r in region_dummies.columns]]

vif1 = pd.Series(
    [variance_inflation_factor(np.column_stack([np.ones(len(X1)), X1]), i + 1) for i in range(X1.shape[1])],
    index=names1, name="VIF",
)
ols1 = OLS(y_edi, X1, w=w, names=names1, y_name="edi")
sar1 = SpatialLag(y_edi, X1, w, names=names1, y_name="edi")
sem1 = SpatialError(y_edi, X1, w, names=names1, y_name="edi")
comp1 = compare_models({"OLS": ols1, "Spatial lag": sar1, "Spatial error": sem1})
display(Markdown("### Model comparison"))
display(comp1.style.format({"loglik": "{:.1f}", "aic": "{:.1f}", "bic": "{:.1f}", "pseudo_r2": "{:.3f}",
                            "rho": "{:.3f}", "lambda": "{:.3f}", "resid_moran_I": "{:.3f}", "resid_moran_p": "{:.3g}"},
                           na_rep=""))
lm1 = ols1.lm_tests()
display(Markdown("### Lagrange Multiplier tests on the OLS residuals"))
display(lm1.to_frame().set_index("test").style.format({"statistic": "{:.1f}", "p_value": "{:.3g}"}))

best1_name = comp1["aic"].idxmin()
best1 = {"OLS": ols1, "Spatial lag": sar1, "Spatial error": sem1}[best1_name]
coef1 = pd.DataFrame({
    "VIF": vif1,
    "OLS beta": np.asarray(ols1.beta)[1:], "OLS p": np.asarray(ols1.pvals)[1:],
    f"{best1_name} beta": np.asarray(best1.beta)[1:], f"{best1_name} p": np.asarray(best1.pvals)[1:],
})
coef1.index = [LABELS.get(n, n.replace("region_", "Region: ")) for n in names1]
display(Markdown("### Coefficients (EDI units per SD of a continuous predictor, or versus the Northeast)"))
display(coef1.style.format({"VIF": "{:.2f}", "OLS beta": "{:+.3f}", "OLS p": "{:.4f}",
                            f"{best1_name} beta": "{:+.3f}", f"{best1_name} p": "{:.4f}"}))

counties["m1_resid"] = np.asarray(ols1.residuals)
cont = coef1.iloc[: len(DEMOG)]
top1 = cont[f"{best1_name} beta"].abs().sort_values(ascending=False).index[:3]
flip = [i for i in coef1.index if np.sign(coef1.loc[i, "OLS beta"]) != np.sign(coef1.loc[i, f"{best1_name} beta"])]
display(Markdown(
    f"Demography and region explain **{ols1.r2 * 100:.0f}%** of the county variance in the EDI by OLS, but the residuals are strongly "
    f"autocorrelated (Moran's I = **{comp1.loc['OLS', 'resid_moran_I']:.3f}**). **{best1_name}** has the lowest AIC "
    f"(spatial parameter **{(best1.rho if hasattr(best1, 'rho') else best1.lam):.2f}**) and leaves residual Moran's I at "
    f"**{comp1.loc[best1_name, 'resid_moran_I']:.3f}**. In that model the largest standardized coefficients are "
    + ", ".join(f"**{i}** ({cont.loc[i, f'{best1_name} beta']:+.2f})" for i in top1)
    + ". "
    + (f"Coefficients that change sign between OLS and the spatial model: **{', '.join(flip)}**. " if flip else "No coefficient changes sign between OLS and the spatial model. ")
    + "These are descriptive correlates of deprivation, not causes."
))

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
text:
Model 2: deprivation and health (H3)
\[Health_i = f(EDI_i, \text{demography, environment, access})\]
Diabetes prevalence is the main outcome, as the guideline recommends. Predictors are the EDI, rural share, share aged 65 and older, PM2.5, and the uninsured rate, all standardized. Four models are fitted in sequence: OLS, spatial lag (SAR), spatial error (SEM), and spatial Durbin (SDM). They are compared by log-likelihood, AIC, residual Moran’s I, and likelihood-ratio tests, and the Durbin model is read through its direct, indirect, and total impacts and not through raw coefficients.


Code
X2 = standardize(counties[M2_PREDICTORS])
y2 = counties["diabetes_pct"].to_numpy(float)
vif2 = pd.Series(
    [variance_inflation_factor(np.column_stack([np.ones(len(X2)), X2]), i + 1) for i in range(X2.shape[1])],
    index=[LABELS[c] for c in M2_PREDICTORS], name="VIF",
)
display(vif2.to_frame().T.style.format("{:.2f}"))

ols2 = OLS(y2, X2, w=w, names=M2_PREDICTORS, y_name="diabetes_pct")
sar2 = SpatialLag(y2, X2, w, names=M2_PREDICTORS, y_name="diabetes_pct")
sem2 = SpatialError(y2, X2, w, names=M2_PREDICTORS, y_name="diabetes_pct")
sdm2 = SpatialDurbin(y2, X2, w, names=M2_PREDICTORS, y_name="diabetes_pct")
models2 = {"OLS": ols2, "Spatial lag": sar2, "Spatial error": sem2, "Spatial Durbin": sdm2}
comp2 = compare_models(models2)
display(Markdown("### Model comparison"))
display(comp2.style.format({"loglik": "{:.1f}", "aic": "{:.1f}", "bic": "{:.1f}", "pseudo_r2": "{:.3f}",
                            "rho": "{:.3f}", "lambda": "{:.3f}", "resid_moran_I": "{:.3f}", "resid_moran_p": "{:.3g}"},
                           na_rep=""))

bp = ols2.breusch_pagan()
lm2 = ols2.lm_tests()
lr_rows = [
    {"restricted": "Spatial lag", "full": "Spatial Durbin", **lr_test(sar2, sdm2)},
    {"restricted": "Spatial error", "full": "Spatial Durbin", **lr_test(sem2, sdm2)},
]

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
section: Does the deprivation-health relationship vary by region? (H4)
text:
Does the deprivation-health relationship vary by region? (H4)
Three local methods from the guideline are applied to the EDI and diabetes.

Geographically weighted correlation (GWCORR): the correlation between EDI and diabetes within each county’s neighborhood.
GWR: the Model 2 regression with coefficients that vary over space, using an adaptive bisquare kernel and a small grid of neighbor counts chosen by AICc.
MGWR: a separate bandwidth for each predictor, fitted with the PySAL mgwr package for five Deep South states (the search is slow for all counties). The cell is skipped if mgwr is not installed.

Local coefficients are less reliable where counties are large and sparse, so the West is read with more caution.


Code
gw = GWSS(bandwidth=150, fixed=False, kernel="bisquare")
gw.fit(counties[["edi", "diabetes_pct"]].to_numpy(float), coords, var_names=["edi", "diabetes"])
counties["gw_corr"] = gw.local_corr_["edi-diabetes"]

gwr_rows, gwr_fits = [], {}
for k in (100, 200, 400):
    fit = GWR(bandwidth=k, fixed=False, kernel="bisquare", criterion="AICc", hat_matrix=True, n_jobs=-1)
    fit.fit(X2, y2, coords)
    gwr_fits[k] = fit
    gwr_rows.append({"k": k, "aicc": fit.aicc_, "rmse": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(fit.residuals_ ** 2)))})
gwr_grid = pd.DataFrame(gwr_rows).sort_values("aicc").reset_index(drop=True)
display(gwr_grid.round(2))
best_k = int(gwr_grid.loc[0, "k"])
gwr = gwr_fits[best_k]
edi_idx = 1 + M2_PREDICTORS.index("edi")
counties["gwr_edi"] = gwr.coef_[:, edi_idx]
counties["gwr_edi_p"] = gwr.p_values_[:, edi_idx]
moran_gwr = Moran(gwr.residuals_, w, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 4.6), constrained_layout=True, dpi=110)
counties.plot(column="gw_corr", cmap="Reds", legend=True,
              ax=axes[0], edgecolor="none", legend_kwds={"shrink": 0.55, "label": "Local correlation"})
axes[0].set_title("GW correlation: EDI and diabetes (150 neighbors)")
lim = float(np.nanpercentile(np.abs(counties["gwr_edi"]), 98))
norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-lim, vcenter=0, vmax=lim)
counties.plot(column="gwr_edi", cmap="RdBu_r", norm=norm, legend=True, ax=axes[1], edgecolor="none",
              legend_kwds={"shrink": 0.55, "label": "pp diabetes per SD EDI"})
axes[1].set_title(f"GWR local EDI coefficient (k = {best_k})")
counties.plot(color="#e0e0e0", ax=axes[2], edgecolor="none")
counties[counties["gwr_edi_p"] < ALPHA].plot(column="gwr_edi", cmap="RdBu_r", norm=norm, legend=True, ax=axes[2],
                                               edgecolor="none", legend_kwds={"shrink": 0.55, "label": "pp diabetes per SD EDI"})
axes[2].set_title(f"Local EDI coefficient where p < {ALPHA} (uncorrected)")
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_axis_off()
plt.show()

counties["area_group"] = np.where(counties["STATE"].isin(MGWR_STATES), "Deep South (5 states)", counties["region"])
reg_tbl = counties.groupby("area_group").agg(
    counties=("gwr_edi", "size"), gw_corr_median=("gw_corr", "median"),
    edi_coef_q25=("gwr_edi", lambda s: s.quantile(0.25)), edi_coef_median=("gwr_edi", "median"),
    edi_coef_q75=("gwr_edi", lambda s: s.quantile(0.75)),
    pct_significant=("gwr_edi_p", lambda s: 100 * (s < ALPHA).mean()),
).sort_values("edi_coef_median", ascending=False)
display(reg_tbl.style.format({"gw_corr_median": "{:.2f}", "edi_coef_q25": "{:.2f}", "edi_coef_median": "{:.2f}",
                              "edi_coef_q75": "{:.2f}", "pct_significant": "{:.0f}"}))

global_edi = float(np.asarray(ols2.beta)[1])
display(Markdown(
    f"GWR with **{best_k}** neighbors lowers the RMSE to **{gwr_grid.loc[0, 'rmse']:.2f}** pp (OLS: {np.sqrt(np.mean(np.asarray(ols2.residuals) ** 2)):.2f}) "
    f"and leaves residual Moran's I at **{moran_gwr.I:.3f}**. The local EDI coefficient ranges from **{counties['gwr_edi'].min():.2f}** to "
    f"**{counties['gwr_edi'].max():.2f}** pp per SD around a global OLS value of **{global_edi:.2f}**; it is positive in "
    f"**{(counties['gwr_edi'] > 0).mean() * 100:.0f}%** of counties and has uncorrected p < {ALPHA} in **{(counties['gwr_edi_p'] < ALPHA).mean() * 100:.0f}%**. "
    f"The median coefficient is highest in the **{reg_tbl.index[0]}** (**{reg_tbl['edi_coef_median'].iloc[0]:.2f}**) and lowest in the "
    f"**{reg_tbl.index[-1]}** (**{reg_tbl['edi_coef_median'].iloc[-1]:.2f}**). The local correlation ranges from "
    f"**{counties['gw_corr'].min():.2f}** to **{counties['gw_corr'].max():.2f}**. H4 is supported: the association is positive almost everywhere but its size varies by a wide margin."
))

        index=[f"GWR (k={int(bw_gwr_r)})", "MGWR"],

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
section: Machine learning as a complementary analysis
text:
Machine learning as a complementary analysis
Five models predict diabetes prevalence from the EDI, demography, PM2.5, and the uninsured rate: linear regression, ridge, elastic net, random forest, and XGBoost. Each is evaluated twice: with ordinary random 5-fold cross-validation, and with folds that hold out whole states. The guideline’s warning is that random splits put neighboring, similar counties in both the training and the test set, so the gap between the two columns measures that optimism. TreeSHAP (from XGBoost’s pred_contribs) describes what drives the predictions. LightGBM, also named in the guideline, is left out to avoid another dependency.


Code
ML_FEATURES = ["edi", *DEMOG, "pm25", "uninsured_pct"]
Xm = counties[ML_FEATURES].to_numpy(float)
groups = counties["STATE"].to_numpy()
xgb_params = dict(n_estimators=400, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8,
                  colsample_bytree=0.8, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=-1)
ML_MODELS = {
    "Linear regression": lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LinearRegression()),
    "Ridge": lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), RidgeCV(alphas=np.logspace(-3, 3, 25))),
    "Elastic net": lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), ElasticNetCV(l1_ratio=[0.2, 0.5, 0.8], cv=5, random_state=SEED)),
    "Random forest": lambda: RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=300, min_samples_leaf=3, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=-1),
    "XGBoost": lambda: xgb.XGBRegressor(**xgb_params),
}
cv_random = KFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=SEED)
cv_state = GroupKFold(n_splits=8)

ml_rows, oof_state = [], {}
sst = np.sum((y2 - y2.mean()) ** 2)
for name, make in ML_MODELS.items():
    p_rand = cross_val_predict(make(), Xm, y2, cv=cv_random)
    p_state = cross_val_predict(make(), Xm, y2, cv=cv_state, groups=groups)
    oof_state[name] = p_state
    ml_rows.append({
        "model": name,
        "R2 random CV": 1 - np.sum((y2 - p_rand) ** 2) / sst,
        "R2 state-blocked CV": 1 - np.sum((y2 - p_state) ** 2) / sst,
        "RMSE random CV": np.sqrt(np.mean((y2 - p_rand) ** 2)),
        "RMSE state-blocked CV": np.sqrt(np.mean((y2 - p_state) ** 2)),
        "MAE state-blocked CV": np.mean(np.abs(y2 - p_state)),
        "resid Moran I (state-blocked)": Moran(y2 - p_state, w, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED).I,
    })
ml_tbl = pd.DataFrame(ml_rows).set_index("model")
ml_tbl["optimism (R2)"] = ml_tbl["R2 random CV"] - ml_tbl["R2 state-blocked CV"]
display(ml_tbl.style.format("{:.3f}"))

xgb_full = xgb.XGBRegressor(**xgb_params).fit(Xm, y2)
shap_vals = xgb_full.get_booster().predict(xgb.DMatrix(Xm), pred_contribs=True)[:, :-1]
shap_imp = pd.Series(np.abs(shap_vals).mean(axis=0), index=[LABELS[c] for c in ML_FEATURES]).sort_values()
counties["shap_edi"] = shap_vals[:, 0]

title: Spatial Inequality and Economic Deprivation in the United States
text:
Decision log








Decision
Choice
Why




Geography
CONUS counties (US_COUNTY.shp)
Geometry available locally; Alaska and Hawaii are not in the shapefile


Period
CHR 2024 release, SVI 2022, Census PEP 2022
Cross-section centered on 2022, with the reference year of every variable tabulated


Missing data
Complete cases; no imputation
Outcomes are not imputed; about 3% of counties are dropped, mostly small ones


EDI components
Six CHR measures: child poverty, unemployment, no diploma, no college, food insecurity, severe housing problems
All point to deprivation after reverse-coding attainment; median income is not in the database


EDI weighting
Equal weights
PCA, leave-one-out, and add-one variants rank counties almost identically


Income inequality
Sensitivity only
The guideline flags its direction as context-dependent


SVI
External check, not an input
Keeps an independent benchmark for the EDI


Weights
Queen with islands linked, row-standardized
Guideline default; Moran’s I checked with KNN-6


Local inference
LISA and bivariate LISA with FDR (9,999 permutations); Gi* analytic with FDR
About 3,000 simultaneous local tests


Inequality measure
Between-state and between-region share of variance
The EDI is a z-score mean, so ratio measures such as the Gini do not apply


Model 1
EDI on demography and region: OLS, SAR, SEM
No EDI component among the predictors


Model 2
Health on EDI, rurality, age, PM2.5, uninsured: OLS, SAR, SEM, SDM
Durbin impacts reported as direct, indirect, and total


Local models
GW correlation, GWR (k in {100, 200, 400}), PySAL MGWR for five Deep South states
MGWR for all counties is slow


Machine learning
Linear, ridge, elastic net, random forest, XGBoost; state-blocked CV
Random splits reported only to show their optimism




Takeaways

Measurement. A six-indicator EDI is internally consistent and robust: PCA weights, dropping any component, or adding income inequality barely change the county ranking, and the index agrees closely with the independently built SVI socioeconomic theme.
Clustering (H1). Deprivation is strongly clustered under both Queen and KNN weights. Food insecurity is the most clustered component and college attainment the least.
Hot spots (H2). After FDR adjustment the High-High counties are almost all in the South (the Texas border, the Mississippi Delta, eastern Kentucky, the Black Belt), and the Low-Low counties are in the upper Midwest and northern Plains.
Between and within. States account for less than half of the county variance in deprivation. Most inequality is between counties of the same state.
What goes with deprivation (Model 1). Population decline and the shares of Hispanic, non-Hispanic Black, and American Indian residents are the strongest correlates. Once spatial dependence is modeled, the Census-region differences are no longer distinguishable from zero.
Deprivation and health (H3). The EDI is associated with higher diabetes prevalence, more premature death, more poor mental health days, and lower life expectancy in every model. For diabetes the association is almost entirely with a county’s own deprivation; the neighboring-county (indirect) part is close to zero.
Geographic variation (H4). The local EDI coefficient is positive everywhere but about twice as large in the Deep South as in the Midwest.
Environmental burden (H5). PM2.5 is only weakly related to deprivation nationally. Deprived counties in the Southeast have high-PM2.5 surroundings, while deprived counties in the mountain West and northern Plains have low-PM2.5 surroundings.
Prediction. Under state-blocked cross-validation the regularized linear models do as well as random forest and XGBoost, and random splits flatter the tree models most. Out-of-fold errors stay spatially autocorrelated for every model.



Extensions (from spatial_inequality.qmd)

Load CDC PLACES, age-adjusted mortality, overdose mortality, and cancer layers into the database and repeat Model 2 for those outcomes.
Add median household income and other ACS measures to the EDI.
Aggregate Superfund proximity and USGS soil geochemistry to counties for a broader test of H5.
Add Alaska and Hawaii with a national county boundary file.
Fit MGWR for all counties and add LightGBM to the model comparison.



Limitations and policy reading
County-level associations are ecological: they describe places, not individuals, and do not establish that deprivation causes the health differences. Several CHR measures are model-based estimates, and food insecurity in particular is modeled partly from poverty and unemployment, which may inflate its correlation with the other components. The rural share is a 2010 Census value. Complete-case filtering removes mainly small counties and all of Connecticut, whose 2022 planning-region FIPS codes do not match the county shapefile. With those limits in mind, the maps point to two policy-relevant facts: deprivation and poor health are concentrated in the same contiguous multi-county areas of the South, which favors regional over county-by-county programs, and large within-state gaps mean that state averages hide many of the most deprived counties.

title: Drug Overdose Mortality - Rate vs Model Rate, and Geographically Weighted Models
text:
Overview

Across contiguous-US counties with complete 2014–2018 overdose records, which geographically weighted model best predicts overdose mortality — and does the ranking change when the target is the raw rate versus the INLA model-based rate?








Step
What we do




Data
Join the CSV to US_COUNTY.shp polygons on FIPS, audit CRS


EDA
Map Rate and Model_Rate, scatter them, summarise by FLAG / urban–rural


Structure
Correlations, VIF, Moran’s I of both outcomes


Models
Fit GWR, GW RF, GW XGBoost, and GNNWR to each outcome


Fair score
Spatial-block (quadrant) cross-validation — not random folds


Local insight
GWR coefficient maps; GW-RF local feature importance


Report
Comparison table, residual maps, decision log



Caveats. County rates are ecological: they do not identify individual risk. Model_Rate is already a spatial smooth, so models that also smooth spatially can look artificially good against it. In-sample (R^2) for tree ensembles is optimistic; trust the spatial-block CV.

text:
Data and CRS
Overdose rates live in the complete-case CSV. County polygons live in US_COUNTY.shp (NAD83 / Conus Albers, metres — EPSG:5070-compatible). We:

Zero-pad FIPS to five characters on both tables.
Inner-join attributes to polygons.
Force EPSG:5070 and wrap the layer in SpatialData.

Analysis coordinates are polygon centroids of the projected geometry (not the CSV x / y columns), so weights, GWR, and maps share one spatial support.


Code
raw = pd.read_csv(CSV)
assert raw.isna().sum().sum() == 0, "Expected a complete-case CSV"
assert set(OUTCOMES).issubset(raw.columns)
assert set(COVARS).issubset(raw.columns)

shp = gpd.read_file(SHP)
raw["fips"] = raw["FIPS"].astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)
shp["fips"] = shp["FIPS"].astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)

# Keep attribute columns from the CSV; geometry and region labels from the shapefile.
attr_cols = ["fips", "State_ABS", "STATE", "COUNTY", "FLAG", "Rate", "Model_Rate",
             "URBAN_RURAL_ID", *COVARS]

unmatched = raw.loc[~raw["fips"].isin(merged["fips"]), ["fips", "COUNTY", "STATE"]]

# Conus Albers already; force a numeric EPSG for downstream code.

    merged = merged.set_crs(5070)
elif merged.crs.to_epsg() != 5070:

    except Exception:

else:

def vif(Z):
    out = []
    for j in range(Z.shape[1]):
        others = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(Z)), np.delete(Z, j, axis=1)])
        beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(others, Z[:, j], rcond=None)
        resid = Z[:, j] - others @ beta
        r2 = 1 - resid.var() / Z[:, j].var()
        out.append(1 / max(1 - r2, 1e-12))
    return np.asarray(out)

text:
Spatial autocorrelation of the outcomes
Before fitting local models, check that both rates are spatially clustered. Queen contiguity is the natural graph for county polygons; any island counties are linked to their nearest non-island neighbour.


Code
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree


def attach_islands(w, xy):
    """Link each island to its nearest non-island county, both ways, then row-standardise."""
    ids = list(w.id_order)
    pos = {i: k for k, i in enumerate(ids)}
    islands = set(w.islands())
    neighbors = {i: list(w.neighbors[i]) for i in ids}
    if not islands:
        return W(neighbors, ids=ids, transform="row")
    tree = cKDTree(xy)
    for isl in islands:
        _, idxs = tree.query(xy[pos[isl]], k=min(25, len(ids)))
        for j in np.atleast_1d(idxs):
            other = ids[int(j)]
            if other == isl or other in islands:
                continue
            if other not in neighbors[isl]:
                neighbors[isl].append(other)
            if isl not in neighbors[other]:
                neighbors[other].append(isl)
            break
    return W(neighbors, ids=ids, transform="row")

title: Drug Overdose Mortality - Rate vs Model Rate, and Geographically Weighted Models
text:
Geographically weighted models
Four local models share the same adaptive bandwidth ((k) = 150 neighbours, bisquare kernel) and the same standardised covariates. Hyperparameters are kept modest so the notebook finishes in a reasonable time:

GWR - local OLS at every county.
GWRandomForest - global RF + local RFs (25 trees, depth 8), blended 50/50.
GWXGBoost - global + local XGBoost (30 trees, depth 3).
GNNWR - Spatially Weighted Neural Network that learns location weights, then local WLS (GPU if available).

In-sample (R^2) for tree ensembles is usually optimistic. Section 7 scores every model with spatial-block CV.


Code
try:
    import torch
    NN_DEVICE = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
except Exception:
    NN_DEVICE = "cpu"


def make_models():
    """Fresh model instances (fit mutates state)."""
    return {
        "GWR": GWR(
            bandwidth=BANDWIDTH, fixed=False, kernel="bisquare",
            criterion="AICc", hat_matrix=False, n_jobs=-1,
        ),
        "GW-RF": GWRandomForest(
            n_estimators=25, max_depth=8, bandwidth=BANDWIDTH, fixed=False,
            kernel="bisquare", local_weight=0.5, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=-1,
        ),
        "GW-XGBoost": GWXGBoost(
            n_estimators=30, max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.1,
            bandwidth=BANDWIDTH, fixed=False, kernel="bisquare",
            local_weight=0.5, n_jobs=-1,
        ),
        "GNNWR": GNNWR(
            hidden_layers=[64, 32], n_epochs=80, batch_size=128, patience=15,
            learning_rate=1e-3, device=NN_DEVICE, random_state=SEED,
        ),
    }


def r2_score(y_true, y_pred):
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, float)
    y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, float)
    return 1.0 - np.sum((y_true - y_pred) ** 2) / np.sum((y_true - y_true.mean()) ** 2)


def rmse(y_true, y_pred):
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean((np.asarray(y_true) - np.asarray(y_pred)) ** 2)))


def fitted_values(model, X_mat, y, coords_mat):
    """In-sample predictions: prefer model.fitted_ / residuals_, else predict()."""
    if getattr(model, "fitted_", None) is not None:
        return np.asarray(model.fitted_, float)
    if getattr(model, "residuals_", None) is not None:
        return y - np.asarray(model.residuals_, float)
    return np.asarray(model.predict(X_mat, coords_mat), float)

print(f"GNNWR device: {NN_DEVICE}")
for outcome in OUTCOMES:
    fits[outcome] = {}
    y = y_vec[outcome]
    print(f"\n=== Fitting models for {outcome} ===")
    for name, model in make_models().items():
        t0 = time.time()

        elapsed = time.time() - t0
        pred = fitted_values(model, X, y, coords)
        fits[outcome][name] = {

text:
Spatial-block cross-validation
Four geographic quadrants by median (x) and (y). Each fold trains on three quadrants and predicts the held-out quadrant. This is the fair comparison: neighbouring counties do not leak into the test fold the way they do under random (k)-fold CV.


Code
mx, my = np.median(coords[:, 0]), np.median(coords[:, 1])
block = (coords[:, 0] > mx).astype(int) * 2 + (coords[:, 1] > my).astype(int)
print("block sizes:", {int(b): int((block == b).sum()) for b in np.unique(block)})


def spatial_cv(outcome, n_jobs_msg=True):
    """Return DataFrame of per-fold and mean R² / RMSE for each model."""
    y = y_vec[outcome]
    records = []
    for name, model0 in make_models().items():
        fold_r2, fold_rmse = [], []
        t0 = time.time()
        for b in sorted(np.unique(block)):
            test = np.where(block == b)[0]
            train = np.where(block != b)[0]
            # Rebuild a fresh model each fold.
            model = make_models()[name]
            model.fit(X[train], y[train], coords[train])
            pred = np.asarray(model.predict(X[test], coords[test]), float)
            fold_r2.append(r2_score(y[test], pred))
            fold_rmse.append(rmse(y[test], pred))
        records.append({
            "outcome": OUTCOMES[outcome], "model": name,
            "cv_R2_mean": float(np.mean(fold_r2)),
            "cv_R2_std": float(np.std(fold_r2)),
            "cv_RMSE_mean": float(np.mean(fold_rmse)),
            "fold_R2": np.round(fold_r2, 3).tolist(),
            "cv_seconds": time.time() - t0,
        })
        if n_jobs_msg:
            print(f"  {outcome:10s} {name:10s}  CV R² = {records[-1]['cv_R2_mean']:.3f} "
                  f"± {records[-1]['cv_R2_std']:.3f}   ({records[-1]['cv_seconds']:.0f}s)")
    return pd.DataFrame(records)


cv_frames = []
print("Spatial-block CV (4 quadrants)")
for outcome in OUTCOMES:
    cv_frames.append(spatial_cv(outcome))

    )
    lim = float(np.nanpercentile(np.abs(resid), 98))
    counties.assign(_r=resid).plot(
        column="_r", cmap="RdBu_r",
        norm=TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-lim, vcenter=0, vmax=lim),
        ax=axes[1, j], edgecolor="none", legend=(j == 3),
        legend_kwds={"label": "residual (obs − pred)", "shrink": 0.6},
    )
    axes[0, j].set_title(f"{name}\npred R² = {fits['Rate'][name]['r2']:.2f}")
    axes[1, j].set_title(f"{name} residuals")
    axes[0, j].set_axis_off(); axes[1, j].set_axis_off()
plt.suptitle("Observed Rate: predictions and residuals", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")

section: Local structure: GWR slopes and GW-RF importances
text:
Local structure: GWR slopes and GW-RF importances
GWR gives a local slope for every covariate. GW-RF gives a local feature-importance surface. Both answer where a relationship is strong, which a single CV score cannot.


Code

gwrf_rate = fits["Rate"]["GW-RF"]["model"]

# GWR local coefficients (column 0 = intercept).
for j, col in enumerate(COVARS):
    counties[f"gwr_{col}"] = gwr_rate.coef_[:, 1 + j]

# Focus on the strongest global OLS correlate with Rate.
focus = corr_y.index[0]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5))

    column=f"gwr_{focus}", cmap="RdBu_r",

)

axes[0].set_title(f"GWR local slope: {COVAR_LABELS[focus]}")

# GW-RF local importances.
if hasattr(gwrf_rate, "feature_importance_map"):

Exploratory. Across 2150 counties, observed overdose Rate and INLA Model_Rate correlate at 0.876. Both are strongly spatial (Moran’s I 0.570 and 0.740). The leading linear correlate of Rate is % COPD.
Model comparison (spatial-block CV). On the raw rate the best model is GNNWR (CV R² = 0.053). On the model-based rate the best model is GW-XGBoost (CV R² = 0.189). GW-RF’s in-sample R² is high but its CV gap is large — local forests can memorise the training neighbourhood. GWR remains the most interpretable option when the scientific question is a local slope, not a black-box prediction. GNNWR is included as the neural geographically weighted alternative; its CV score should be read alongside the known simplicity of the current SWNN training path in geolattice.
Rate vs Model_Rate. Scoring against Model_Rate rewards spatial smoothness. Prefer Rate when the goal is to predict what a vital-statistics office publishes, and Model_Rate when the goal is a precision-aware risk surface.
Limits. Ecological inference; 2014–2018 pooled cross-section; adaptive bandwidth fixed a priori rather than AICc-tuned separately for every ensemble; GNNWR early-stopping and architecture are not exhaustively tuned.

text:
Overview

Across contiguous-U.S. counties, are diabetes, obesity, and premature death spatially clustered? Are economically deprived and socially vulnerable counties more likely to carry higher disease burden? Do socioeconomic associations vary geographically, and which counties combine multiple forms of disadvantage?


Research questions

The cross-sectional sections use one release (CHR 2024 + SVI 2022). The multi-year section uses CHR releases, which are not calendar years and can reuse or re-model the underlying data, so it is read as a stability check and not as an annual trend. section: Data: the USA Health Data Atlas database
text:
Data: the USA Health Data Atlas database
Module 1 of the guideline is data integration. The Atlas SQLite database already holds CHR, SVI, and Census PEP as long county_indicators rows. We first audit which dataset-years are available, then pivot the needed variables to a county-level analysis table and join CONUS polygons on five-digit FIPS. The guideline warns that sources do not share a reference year, so the year of each input is kept explicit in SPEC.


Code

    "pop": ("census_demography", "POP", CENSUS_YEAR),
}
for comp in EDI_COMPONENTS:
    SPEC[comp.lower()] = ("social_vulnerability_index", comp, SVI_YEAR)

params = []
for dataset, variable, year in SPEC.values():
    params.extend([dataset, variable, year])
placeholders = ",".join(["(?, ?, ?)"] * len(SPEC))
indicator_sql = (
    "SELECT i.fips, d.dataset_name, i.variable, i.year, i.value "
    "FROM county_indicators AS i "
    "JOIN dataset_catalog AS d USING (dataset_id) "
    "WHERE (d.dataset_name, i.variable, i.year) IN (" + placeholders + ")"
)
long = pd.read_sql(indicator_sql, con, params=params)
con.close()

wide = long.pivot_table(
    index="fips", columns=["dataset_name", "variable", "year"], values="value"
)
table = pd.DataFrame(index=wide.index.astype(str).str.zfill(5))
for name, (dataset, variable, year) in SPEC.items():
    table[name] = wide[(dataset, variable, year)].to_numpy()

# EDI: equal-weighted mean of aligned SVI percentiles (already 0-1, higher = worse)
edi_cols = [c.lower() for c in EDI_COMPONENTS]
table["edi"] = table[edi_cols].mean(axis=1)

# Scale prevalence outcomes to percent for readable maps/tables
table["diabetes_pct"] = 100 * table["diabetes"]
table["obesity_pct"] = 100 * table["obesity"]

display(table[["diabetes_pct", "obesity_pct", "premature_death", "edi", "svi", "uninsured", "pcp", "pm25", "pct_rural"]].describe().round(3))
display(Markdown(
    f"Extracted **{len(table):,}** county rows. "
    f"Mean diabetes prevalence is **{table['diabetes_pct'].mean():.1f}%**; "
    f"mean EDI is **{table['edi'].mean():.3f}** (SVI percentile scale)."
))

Indicator construction: EDI and Health Disparity Index
EDI is the equal-weighted mean of five SVI deprivation percentiles. HDI is a descriptive composite of standardized diabetes, obesity, premature death, EDI, SVI, uninsured, and PM2.5 (PCP enters inverted so that higher HDI = worse). HDI is for ranking and mapping, not a validated needs score.

    return (s - s.mean()) / s.std(ddof=0)

EDI check: equal weights versus PCA
The guideline suggests comparing the equal-weighted index with a PCA-based one. The first principal component of the five standardized SVI components is a data-driven weighting. If the two indices rank counties almost identically, the simpler equal-weighted EDI is kept for the models.


Code
E = counties[edi_cols].to_numpy(float)
Ez = (E - E.mean(axis=0)) / E.std(axis=0, ddof=0)
_, sing, Vt = np.linalg.svd(Ez, full_matrices=False)
explained = sing ** 2 / np.sum(sing ** 2)
loadings = Vt[0] * np.sign(Vt[0].sum())  # orient so that higher = more deprived
counties["edi_pca"] = Ez @ loadings

load_tbl = pd.DataFrame(
    {"PC1 loading": loadings, "equal weight": 1 / np.sqrt(len(edi_cols))},
    index=EDI_COMPONENTS,
)
display(load_tbl.style.format("{:.3f}"))

rho_edi = spearmanr(counties["edi"], counties["edi_pca"])[0]
top_eq = set(counties.index[counties["edi"] >= counties["edi"].quantile(0.8)])
top_pc = set(counties.index[counties["edi_pca"] >= counties["edi_pca"].quantile(0.8)])
share_top = len(top_eq & top_pc) / len(top_eq)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.8, 4.5), constrained_layout=True)

section: Spatial weights and global Moran’s I
text:
Spatial weights and global Moran’s I
Queen contiguity with nearest-neighbor linking for any islands. Global Moran’s I for each outcome and for EDI tests whether similar values cluster geographically.


Code
def attach_islands(w, xy):
    """Link each island to its nearest non-island county, both ways, then row-standardise."""
    ids = list(w.id_order)
    pos = {i: k for k, i in enumerate(ids)}
    islands = set(w.islands())
    neighbors = {i: list(w.neighbors[i]) for i in ids}
    if not islands:
        return W(neighbors, ids=ids, transform="row")
    tree = cKDTree(xy)
    for isl in islands:
        _, idxs = tree.query(xy[pos[isl]], k=min(25, len(ids)))
        for j in np.atleast_1d(idxs):
            other = ids[int(j)]
            if other == isl or other in islands:
                continue
            if other not in neighbors[isl]:
                neighbors[isl].append(other)
            if isl not in neighbors[other]:
                neighbors[other].append(isl)
            break
    return W(neighbors, ids=ids, transform="row")


w_raw = Queen(counties, transform="row")
w = attach_islands(w_raw, coords)
print(w.summary())
display(Markdown(
    f"Raw Queen had **{len(w_raw.islands())}** island(s); after linking, "
    f"**{len(w.islands())}** remain in **{w.n_components()}** component(s)."
))

moran_targets = {
    "diabetes_pct": "Diabetes %",
    "obesity_pct": "Obesity %",
    "premature_death": "Premature death",
    "edi": "EDI",
    "svi": "SVI",
    "hdi": "HDI",
}
moran_rows = []
morans = {}
for col, label in moran_targets.items():
    mi = Moran(counties[col].to_numpy(float), w, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED)
    morans[col] = mi
    moran_rows.append({"variable": label, "I": mi.I, "z": mi.z_score, "p_value": mi.p_value})
moran_tbl = pd.DataFrame(moran_rows).set_index("variable")
display(moran_tbl.style.format({"I": "{:.3f}", "z": "{:.2f}", "p_value": "{:.4f}"}))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 4), constrained_layout=True)
for ax, col in zip(axes, ["diabetes_pct", "edi", "hdi"]):
    moran_scatter(morans[col], ax=ax, s=8, alpha=0.35)
    ax.set_title(f"{moran_targets[col]}\nI = {morans[col].I:.3f}")

    f"(p = **{morans['diabetes_pct'].p_value:.4f}**), supporting spatial clustering of health burden."

Local clusters: LISA and Gi* for diabetes
Local Moran’s I labels HH / LL / HL / LH clusters. Gi* highlights hot and cold spots. The first map uses uncorrected permutation p-values at alpha = 0.05 alongside analytic Gi*; the next cell applies the false discovery rate correction the guideline recommends for reporting.

LISA with false discovery rate control
Each county is a separate test, so the uncorrected map above overstates the number of clusters. The guideline recommends the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. With FDR the smallest attainable permutation p-value matters, so the local statistic is rerun with more permutations (PERM_LOCAL).

def lisa_fdr_clusters(values):
    # FDR-adjusted LISA. The resolution warning is silenced: it flags that few counties may
    # survive FDR at this permutation count, and the counts reported below show that many do.
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        return local_moran_clusters(
            values, w, permutations=PERM_LOCAL, correction="fdr", alpha=ALPHA, seed=SEED
        )

section: Bivariate spatial association: EDI and diabetes
text:
Bivariate spatial association: EDI and diabetes
Bivariate Moran’s I correlates local EDI with the spatial lag of diabetes (and the reverse), after z-scoring both variables so the statistic is on a correlation-like scale. This asks whether deprived counties sit near high-diabetes neighbors. Bivariate LISA then shows where.


Code
x_edi = counties["edi"].to_numpy(float)
y_diab = counties["diabetes_pct"].to_numpy(float)
# Z-score both sides so bivariate I is on a correlation-like scale
# (raw EDI vs diabetes % mixes 0-1 ranks with percentage points).
x_z = (x_edi - x_edi.mean()) / x_edi.std(ddof=0)
y_z = (y_diab - y_diab.mean()) / y_diab.std(ddof=0)
bv_edi_diab = MoranBV(x_z, y_z, w, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED)
bv_diab_edi = MoranBV(y_z, x_z, w, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED)

text:
Regression models of diabetes disparities
OLS baseline, then spatial lag (SAR), spatial error (SEM), and spatial Durbin (SDM), which adds the neighbors’ predictors (W_x) to the lag model. Predictors: EDI, SVI, uninsured, PCP, PM2.5, and percent rural. Check VIF before fitting.


Code
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor

X_raw = counties[PREDICTORS].to_numpy(dtype=float)
X_std = (X_raw - X_raw.mean(axis=0)) / X_raw.std(axis=0, ddof=0)
y = counties["diabetes_pct"].to_numpy(dtype=float)

vif_tbl = pd.DataFrame({
    "predictor": [PRED_LABELS[c] for c in PREDICTORS],
    "VIF": [variance_inflation_factor(np.column_stack([np.ones(len(X_std)), X_std]), i + 1)
            for i in range(X_std.shape[1])],
}).set_index("predictor")
display(vif_tbl.style.format("{:.2f}"))

ols = OLS(y, X_std, w=w, names=PREDICTORS, y_name="diabetes_pct")
sar = SpatialLag(y, X_std, w, names=PREDICTORS, y_name="diabetes_pct")
sem = SpatialError(y, X_std, w, names=PREDICTORS, y_name="diabetes_pct")
sdm = SpatialDurbin(y, X_std, w, names=PREDICTORS, y_name="diabetes_pct")

comp = compare_models({"OLS": ols, "Spatial lag": sar, "Spatial error": sem, "Spatial Durbin": sdm})

OLS diagnostics, model choice, and spillovers
The guideline asks for heteroskedasticity and residual diagnostics, and for a decision between the lag, error, and Durbin specifications. Lagrange Multiplier tests on the OLS residuals point to the form of spatial dependence, likelihood-ratio tests check whether the Durbin terms (W_x) can be dropped, and the Durbin impacts split each association into a direct (own-county) and an indirect (neighboring-county) part.


Code
bp = ols.breusch_pagan()
jb = ols.jarque_bera()
diag_tbl = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {"diagnostic": "Breusch-Pagan (heteroskedasticity)", "statistic": bp["statistic"], "p_value": bp["p_value"]},
        {"diagnostic": "Jarque-Bera (normality)", "statistic": jb["statistic"], "p_value": jb["p_value"]},
        {"diagnostic": "Condition number", "statistic": ols.condition_number, "p_value": np.nan},
    ]
).set_index("diagnostic")

lr_sem = lr_test(sem, sdm)

    [
        {"restricted": "Spatial lag", "full": "Spatial Durbin", **lr_sar},
        {"restricted": "Spatial error", "full": "Spatial Durbin", **lr_sem},

)

title: Spatial Patterns, Socioeconomic Determinants, and Geographic Inequalities in Health Outcomes Across U.S. Counties
text:
Geographically weighted regression
GWR lets the EDI-diabetes slope vary across counties. A coarse adaptive-bandwidth grid picks the AICc-minimizing neighbor count. MGWR then relaxes the single-bandwidth assumption for one region.


Code
gwr_rows, gwr_fits = [], {}
for k in (100, 200, 400):
    fit = GWR(
        bandwidth=k, fixed=False, kernel="bisquare",
        criterion="AICc", hat_matrix=True, n_jobs=-1,
    )
    fit.fit(X_std, y, coords)
    gwr_fits[k] = fit
    gwr_rows.append({
        "k": k,
        "aicc": fit.aicc_,
        "rmse": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(fit.residuals_ ** 2))),
    })
gwr_grid = pd.DataFrame(gwr_rows).sort_values("aicc").reset_index(drop=True)
display(gwr_grid.round(2))
best_k = int(gwr_grid.loc[0, "k"])
gwr = gwr_fits[best_k]

# coef_ column 0 = intercept; predictors follow PREDICTORS order
edi_idx = 1 + PREDICTORS.index("edi")
counties["gwr_edi"] = gwr.coef_[:, edi_idx]
local_p = gwr.p_values_[:, edi_idx]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5), constrained_layout=True)
lim = float(np.nanpercentile(np.abs(counties["gwr_edi"]), 98))
counties.plot(
    column="gwr_edi", cmap="RdBu_r",
    norm=TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-lim, vcenter=0, vmax=lim),
    legend=True, ax=axes[0], edgecolor="none",
    legend_kwds={"shrink": 0.6, "label": "Local EDI slope"},
)
axes[0].set_title(f"GWR EDI coefficient on diabetes (k={best_k})")

MGWR: covariate-specific scales in the Deep South
GWR forces one bandwidth on every coefficient. MGWR estimates a separate bandwidth for each predictor, so a process that is nearly regional can be told apart from one that changes over short distances. This cell uses the PySAL mgwr package, the Python MGWR library named in the guideline, because its back-fitting bandwidth search and local standard errors are well tested. The search is slow for about 2,900 counties, so the model is fitted to the five Deep South states that hold most High-High diabetes counties (MGWR_STATES). Predictors are re-standardized within the region, which makes the bandwidths comparable across terms. The cell is skipped if mgwr is not installed.


Code
try:
    from mgwr.gwr import GWR as PysalGWR, MGWR as PysalMGWR
    from mgwr.sel_bw import Sel_BW
    HAVE_MGWR = True
except ImportError:
    HAVE_MGWR = False
    print("mgwr is not installed (pip install mgwr); the MGWR section is skipped.")

if HAVE_MGWR:
    in_region = counties["STATE"].isin(MGWR_STATES).to_numpy()
    region = counties.loc[in_region].copy()
    Xr = X_raw[in_region]
    Xr = (Xr - Xr.mean(axis=0)) / Xr.std(axis=0, ddof=0)
    yr = y[in_region].reshape(-1, 1)
    cr = coords[in_region]

    bw_gwr_r = Sel_BW(cr, yr, Xr).search()
    gwr_r = PysalGWR(cr, yr, Xr, bw_gwr_r).fit()
    mgwr_sel = Sel_BW(cr, yr, Xr, multi=True)
    mgwr_bws = mgwr_sel.search()
    mgwr_fit = PysalMGWR(cr, yr, Xr, mgwr_sel).fit()

    terms = ["Intercept", *[PRED_LABELS[c] for c in PREDICTORS]]
    t_filtered = mgwr_fit.filter_tvals()  # zero where not significant after the multiple-testing correction
    bw_tbl = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "bandwidth (neighbors)": np.asarray(mgwr_bws, dtype=int),
            "share of region": np.asarray(mgwr_bws, dtype=float) / len(region),
            "effective params": mgwr_fit.ENP_j,
            "coef min": mgwr_fit.params.min(axis=0),
            "coef median": np.median(mgwr_fit.params, axis=0),
            "coef max": mgwr_fit.params.max(axis=0),
            "% counties significant": 100 * (t_filtered != 0).mean(axis=0),
        },
        index=terms,
    )
    display(bw_tbl.style.format({
        "share of region": "{:.0%}", "effective params": "{:.1f}", "coef min": "{:.2f}",
        "coef median": "{:.2f}", "coef max": "{:.2f}", "% counties significant": "{:.0f}",
    }))
    fit_tbl = pd.DataFrame(
        {"AICc": [gwr_r.aicc, mgwr_fit.aicc], "R2": [gwr_r.R2, mgwr_fit.R2],
         "effective params": [gwr_r.ENP, mgwr_fit.ENP]},
        index=[f"GWR (k={int(bw_gwr_r)})", "MGWR"],
    )
    display(fit_tbl.style.format({"AICc": "{:.1f}", "R2": "{:.3f}", "effective params": "{:.1f}"}))

    region["gwr_edi_r"] = gwr_r.params[:, edi_idx]
    region["mgwr_edi"] = mgwr_fit.params[:, edi_idx]
    lim = float(np.nanpercentile(np.abs(region[["gwr_edi_r", "mgwr_edi"]].to_numpy()), 98))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.6), constrained_layout=True)
    for ax, col, title in [
        (axes[0], "gwr_edi_r", f"GWR EDI slope (one bandwidth, k={int(bw_gwr_r)})"),
        (axes[1], "mgwr_edi", f"MGWR EDI slope (k={int(mgwr_bws[edi_idx])})"),
    ]:
        region.plot(
            column=col, cmap="RdBu_r", norm=TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-lim, vcenter=0, vmax=lim),
            legend=True, ax=ax, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.1,
            legend_kwds={"shrink": 0.6, "label": "pp diabetes per SD EDI"},
        )
        ax.set_title(title)
        ax.set_axis_off()
    plt.show()

    local_terms = bw_tbl.index[bw_tbl["share of region"] < 0.25].tolist()
    broad_terms = bw_tbl.index[bw_tbl["share of region"] > 0.75].tolist()
    display(Markdown(
        f"Region: **{len(region)}** counties in {', '.join(MGWR_STATES)}. "
        f"The single GWR bandwidth is **{int(bw_gwr_r)}** neighbors; MGWR bandwidths range from "
        f"**{int(min(mgwr_bws))}** to **{int(max(mgwr_bws))}**. "
        f"Short-range terms (under 25% of the region): **{', '.join(local_terms) or 'none'}**. "
        f"Near-regional terms (over 75%): **{', '.join(broad_terms) or 'none'}**. "
        f"AICc is **{mgwr_fit.aicc:.1f}** for MGWR and **{gwr_r.aicc:.1f}** for GWR. "
        f"The EDI slope is significant in **{bw_tbl.loc[PRED_LABELS['edi'], '% counties significant']:.0f}%** "
        f"of the region's counties after the MGWR multiple-testing correction."
    ))

title: Spatial Patterns, Socioeconomic Determinants, and Geographic Inequalities in Health Outcomes Across U.S. Counties
text:
Explainable machine learning (XGBoost + TreeSHAP)
State-grouped cross-validation avoids leaking neighboring counties across folds. TreeSHAP contributions (pred_contribs) summarize nonlinear feature importance for diabetes prevalence.


Code
params = dict(
    n_estimators=400, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.05,
    subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=-1,
)
groups = counties["STATE"].to_numpy()
oof = np.full(len(y), np.nan)
for train, test in GroupKFold(n_splits=8).split(X_raw, y, groups):
    model = xgb.XGBRegressor(**params).fit(X_raw[train], y[train])
    oof[test] = model.predict(X_raw[test])

ss_res = np.sum((y - oof) ** 2)
r2_cv = 1 - ss_res / np.sum((y - y.mean()) ** 2)

oof_ols = np.full(len(y), np.nan)
for train, test in GroupKFold(n_splits=8).split(X_std, y, groups):
    A = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(train)), X_std[train]])
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, y[train], rcond=None)
    oof_ols[test] = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(test)), X_std[test]]) @ beta
r2_cv_ols = 1 - np.sum((y - oof_ols) ** 2) / np.sum((y - y.mean()) ** 2)

xgb_model = xgb.XGBRegressor(**params).fit(X_raw, y)
shap_vals = xgb_model.get_booster().predict(
    xgb.DMatrix(X_raw), pred_contribs=True
)[:, :-1]
shap_imp = pd.Series(
    np.abs(shap_vals).mean(axis=0),
    index=[PRED_LABELS[c] for c in PREDICTORS],
).sort_values()

resid_ml = y - oof
moran_ml = Moran(resid_ml, w, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.8), constrained_layout=True)
axes[0].barh(shap_imp.index, shap_imp.values, color="#6B5B95")
axes[0].set_xlabel("mean |SHAP| (pp diabetes)")
axes[0].set_title("XGBoost feature importance")
top_feat = PREDICTORS[int(np.argmax(np.abs(shap_vals).mean(axis=0)))]
counties[f"shap_{top_feat}"] = shap_vals[:, PREDICTORS.index(top_feat)]
lim = float(np.nanpercentile(np.abs(counties[f"shap_{top_feat}"]), 98))
counties.plot(
    column=f"shap_{top_feat}", cmap="RdBu_r",
    norm=TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-lim, vcenter=0, vmax=lim),
    legend=True, ax=axes[1], edgecolor="none",
    legend_kwds={"shrink": 0.6, "label": "SHAP (pp)"},
)
axes[1].set_axis_off()
axes[1].set_title(f"Where {PRED_LABELS[top_feat]} pushed predicted diabetes")
plt.show()

display(Markdown(
    f"State-held-out R$^2$: XGBoost **{r2_cv:.2f}** vs standardized OLS **{r2_cv_ols:.2f}**. "
    f"Residual Moran I of out-of-fold errors = **{moran_ml.I:.3f}** "
    f"(p = **{moran_ml.p_value:.4f}**). "
    f"Top TreeSHAP features: "
    + ", ".join(f"**{lab}**" for lab in shap_imp.index[::-1][:3])
    + "."
))









State-held-out R\(^2\): XGBoost 0.73 vs standardized OLS 0.70. Residual Moran I of out-of-fold errors = 0.429 (p = 0.0010). Top TreeSHAP features: Economic deprivation (EDI), SVI overall, % uninsured.

section: Multiple years: a CHR release panel
text:
Multiple years: a CHR release panel
The guideline’s Section 11 extends the analysis to several years. The Atlas database holds six CHR releases (2020 to 2025). Before building a panel we check that the diabetes series is comparable across releases, then ask three questions: is the clustering stable, are the hot spots the same counties each year, and does the deprivation association survive county and year fixed effects?
Two cautions from the guideline apply. A CHR release is not a calendar year: each release reports the latest available data, some measures repeat across releases, and model-based estimates can change with the method. Inputs derived from ACS 5-year files overlap across adjacent years. The panel is therefore a stability check, not an annual trend analysis.


Code
PANEL_VARS = {
    "diabetes": "Diabetes Prevalence",
    "uninsured": "Uninsured",
    "children_poverty": "Children in Poverty",
    "unemployment": "Unemployment",
}
con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
marks = ",".join("?" * len(PANEL_VARS))
panel_long = pd.read_sql(
    "SELECT i.fips, i.year, i.variable, i.value "
    "FROM county_indicators AS i JOIN dataset_catalog AS d USING (dataset_id) "
    f"WHERE d.dataset_name = 'county_health_rankings' AND i.variable IN ({marks})",
    con, params=list(PANEL_VARS.values()),
)
con.close()
panel_long["fips"] = panel_long["fips"].astype(str).str.zfill(5)
panel_long["variable"] = panel_long["variable"].map({v: k for k, v in PANEL_VARS.items()})
panel_long["value"] = 100 * panel_long["value"]  # proportions -> percent

# 1) Comparability of the diabetes series across all releases
diab_wide = (
    panel_long[panel_long["variable"] == "diabetes"]
    .pivot(index="fips", columns="year", values="value")
    .reindex(counties["fips"])
)
years_all = list(diab_wide.columns)
compar = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "mean_pct": diab_wide.mean(),
        "corr_with_previous_release": [np.nan] + [
            diab_wide[a].corr(diab_wide[b]) for a, b in zip(years_all[:-1], years_all[1:])
        ],
    }
)
compar.index.name = "CHR release"
display(compar.style.format({"mean_pct": "{:.2f}", "corr_with_previous_release": "{:.3f}"}, na_rep=""))
weakest = compar["corr_with_previous_release"].idxmin()
display(Markdown(
    f"The weakest link is between releases **{weakest - 1}** and **{weakest}** "
    f"(r = **{compar['corr_with_previous_release'].min():.2f}**), a break that points to a change in how the "
    f"estimate was produced and not to a real one-year shift. The panel uses releases "
    f"**{PANEL_YEARS[0]} to {PANEL_YEARS[-1]}**, where adjacent releases correlate above "
    f"**{compar.loc[PANEL_YEARS[1]:, 'corr_with_previous_release'].min():.2f}**."
))

# 2) Balanced panel on the study counties (same order as `counties`, so `w` applies to every year)
panel = (
    panel_long[panel_long["year"].isin(PANEL_YEARS)]
    .pivot_table(index=["fips", "year"], columns="variable", values="value")
    .reset_index()
)
complete = panel.dropna().groupby("fips")["year"].nunique()
keep = set(complete.index[complete == len(PANEL_YEARS)])
panel_ok = counties["fips"].isin(keep).to_numpy()
print(f"balanced panel: {int(panel_ok.sum()):,} of {len(counties):,} study counties x {len(PANEL_YEARS)} releases")
assert panel_ok.all(), "panel does not cover every study county; rebuild weights on the subset"

diab_panel = diab_wide[PANEL_YEARS].to_numpy(float)

# 3) Moran's I and FDR-adjusted High-High clusters by release
year_rows, hh_by_year = [], {}
for j, yr_ in enumerate(PANEL_YEARS):
    v = diab_panel[:, j]
    mi_t = Moran(v, w, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED)
    li_t = lisa_fdr_clusters(v)
    hh_by_year[yr_] = np.asarray(li_t.labels) == "HH"
    year_rows.append({
        "CHR release": yr_, "mean_pct": v.mean(), "sd_pct": v.std(),
        "moran_I": mi_t.I, "p_value": mi_t.p_value, "HH_counties": int(hh_by_year[yr_].sum()),
    })
year_tbl = pd.DataFrame(year_rows).set_index("CHR release")
display(year_tbl.style.format({
    "mean_pct": "{:.2f}", "sd_pct": "{:.2f}", "moran_I": "{:.3f}", "p_value": "{:.4f}",
}))

Hot-spot persistence and change
Counting the releases in which a county is an FDR-significant High-High county gives a simple version of emerging hot-spot analysis: persistent (every release), new (High-High in the last release but not the first), former (the reverse), and sporadic.


Code
hh_mat = np.column_stack([hh_by_year[t] for t in PANEL_YEARS])
n_hh = hh_mat.sum(axis=1)
first, last = hh_mat[:, 0], hh_mat[:, -1]
trend = np.full(len(counties), "Never High-High", dtype=object)
trend[n_hh > 0] = "Sporadic"
trend[first & ~last] = "Former"
trend[~first & last] = "New"
trend[n_hh == len(PANEL_YEARS)] = "Persistent"
counties["hh_trend"] = trend
counties["diab_change"] = diab_panel[:, -1] - diab_panel[:, 0]
mi_change = Moran(counties["diab_change"].to_numpy(float), w, permutations=PERM, seed=SEED)

TREND_COLORS = {
    "Never High-High": "#e0e0e0",
    "Persistent": "#7f0000",
    "New": "#ef6548",
    "Former": "#74a9cf",
    "Sporadic": "#fdbb84",
}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.2), constrained_layout=True)
for label, color in TREND_COLORS.items():
    part = counties[counties["hh_trend"] == label]
    if len(part):
        part.plot(ax=axes[0], color=color, edgecolor="none", linewidth=0)
axes[0].legend(
    handles=[Patch(color=c, label=l) for l, c in TREND_COLORS.items()],
    loc="lower left", fontsize=8, frameon=False,
)
axes[0].set_title(f"Diabetes High-High clusters, CHR {PANEL_YEARS[0]}-{PANEL_YEARS[-1]}")
axes[0].set_axis_off()

    column="diab_change", cmap="RdBu_r", norm=TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-lim, vcenter=0, vmax=lim),
    legend=True, ax=axes[1], edgecolor="none",
    legend_kwds={"shrink": 0.6, "label": "Change in prevalence (pp)"},
)
axes[1].set_title(f"Change in diabetes prevalence, release {PANEL_YEARS[0]} to {PANEL_YEARS[-1]}")
axes[1].set_axis_off()
plt.show()

trend_tbl = counties["hh_trend"].value_counts().reindex(list(TREND_COLORS), fill_value=0)
display(trend_tbl.rename_axis("class").reset_index(name="n"))
ever = int((n_hh > 0).sum())
display(Markdown(
    f"Moran's I stays between **{year_tbl['moran_I'].min():.3f}** and **{year_tbl['moran_I'].max():.3f}** across releases. "
    f"Of the **{ever}** counties that are High-High at least once, **{int(trend_tbl['Persistent'])}** "
    f"(**{trend_tbl['Persistent'] / ever * 100:.0f}%**) are High-High in every release. "
    f"The change between the first and last release is itself spatially clustered "
    f"(Moran's I = **{mi_change.I:.3f}**, p = **{mi_change.p_value:.4f}**), which for a model-based "
    f"estimate can reflect regional revisions as much as real change."
